theory.title: Introduction to BuiltIn Library Keywords
theory.content:
## The BuiltIn Library

The **BuiltIn library** is Robot Framework's most fundamental library, containing keywords that are automatically available in every test suite without explicit import. It provides essential functionality for:

- **Logging and debugging:** Log, Log Many, Log To Console
- **Variable operations:** Set Variable, Set Test Variable, Set Suite Variable
- **Time management:** Sleep, Wait Until Keyword Succeeds
- **Control flow:** Run Keyword If, Return From Keyword
- **Assertions:** Should Be Equal, Should Contain, Should Be True

### Why BuiltIn Matters

Unlike external libraries (SeleniumLibrary, RequestsLibrary, etc.) that must be imported, BuiltIn keywords are **always available**. This makes them the foundation of Robot Framework testing—you'll use BuiltIn keywords in virtually every test you write.

## The Log Keyword

`Log` outputs messages to execution logs, making it invaluable for debugging and tracking test execution.

### Syntax

```robot
Log    message
Log    message    log_level
Log    message    log_level    html=True
```

**Parameters:**
- `message`: Text or variable to log (required)
- `log_level`: INFO (default), WARN, ERROR, DEBUG, TRACE
- `html`: Set to True to render HTML in message

### Log Levels

```robot
Log    Normal information    INFO
Log    Warning message       WARN
Log    Error occurred        ERROR
Log    Debug details         DEBUG
```

Log levels control visibility in reports:
- **INFO:** Always visible (default)
- **WARN:** Highlighted in yellow
- **ERROR:** Highlighted in red (doesn't fail test)
- **DEBUG/TRACE:** Hidden by default, shown with --loglevel

### Logging Variables

```robot
${count}    Set Variable    10
Log    Count is: ${count}    # Logs: Count is: 10
Log    ${count}              # Logs: 10
```

Variables are **substituted** before logging, so you see the actual value.

## The Sleep Keyword

`Sleep` pauses test execution for a specified duration.

### Syntax

```robot
Sleep    time
Sleep    time    reason
```

**Time formats:**
- Seconds: `1s`, `0.5s`, `2.5s`
- Milliseconds: `500ms`, `1000ms`
- Minutes: `1min`, `2.5min`
- Hours: `1h`, `0.5h`
- Plain numbers: Interpreted as seconds (`1` = 1 second)

### Examples

```robot
Sleep    1s                        # Sleep 1 second
Sleep    500ms                     # Sleep 0.5 seconds
Sleep    2.5s                      # Sleep 2.5 seconds
Sleep    1min                      # Sleep 60 seconds
Sleep    1s    Waiting for animation    # With reason (shown in log)
```

### When to Use Sleep

**Appropriate uses:**
```robot
# Waiting for known animation duration
Click Button    id:submit
Sleep    500ms    UI animation duration
Element Should Be Visible    id:success-message

# Rate limiting API calls
FOR    ${i}    IN RANGE    10
    Make API Call
    Sleep    1s    API rate limit: 1 req/sec
END
```

**Inappropriate uses (use explicit waits instead):**
```robot
# Bad: Arbitrary wait hoping page loads
Click Button    id:submit
Sleep    5s    # What if page loads in 2s? What if it takes 10s?

# Good: Wait for specific condition
Click Button    id:submit
Wait Until Page Contains    Success    timeout=10s
```

**Golden rule:** Prefer explicit waits (`Wait Until...`) over arbitrary sleeps.

## The Set Variable Keyword

`Set Variable` assigns a value to a variable at runtime.

### Syntax

```robot
${variable}    Set Variable    value
${variable}    Set Variable    ${other_variable}
${variable}    Set Variable    ${expression}
```

### Basic Assignment

```robot
${name}      Set Variable    Alice
${age}       Set Variable    30
${active}    Set Variable    ${True}
${count}     Set Variable    ${10}
```

### Copying Variables

```robot
${original}    Set Variable    Hello
${copy}        Set Variable    ${original}
Log    ${copy}    # Logs: Hello
```

### Variable Types

```robot
# String
${text}    Set Variable    Hello World

# Number (as string by default)
${num}     Set Variable    42

# Number (explicit type)
${num}     Set Variable    ${42}

# Boolean
${flag}    Set Variable    ${True}
${flag}    Set Variable    ${False}

# List
${items}    Create List    apple    banana    orange

# Dictionary
${user}     Create Dictionary    name=Alice    age=30
```

## Variable Scope in This Exercise

Variables created with `Set Variable` are **test-scoped** by default—they exist only within the test case where they're created:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Test 1
    ${status}    Set Variable    Complete
    Log    ${status}    # Works: Variable exists

Test 2
    Log    ${status}    # FAILS: Variable doesn't exist here
```

For broader scope:
- **Suite scope:** `Set Suite Variable    ${var}    value`
- **Global scope:** `Set Global Variable    ${var}    value`
- **Variables section:** `${VAR}    value` (suite-scoped)

## Combining Keywords in Sequence

This exercise demonstrates **sequential execution**—keywords run top-to-bottom, one after another:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
BuiltIn Keywords Test
    Log    Starting test       # Step 1: Log message
    Sleep    1s                # Step 2: Wait 1 second
    ${status}    Set Variable    Complete    # Step 3: Create variable
    Log    ${status}           # Step 4: Log variable value
```

**Execution flow:**
1. Log "Starting test" to log.html
2. Pause for 1 second
3. Create variable `${status}` with value "Complete"
4. Log "Complete" to log.html
5. Test passes (no assertions, all keywords succeeded)

## Why These Keywords Matter

These three keywords form the foundation of Robot Framework automation:

- **Log:** Visibility into test execution (debugging)
- **Sleep:** Time management and synchronization
- **Set Variable:** Data manipulation and state tracking

You'll use these keywords constantly, often in combination with library-specific keywords:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
User Registration Flow
    Log    Starting registration test    # BuiltIn
    Open Browser    https://app.com    Chrome    # SeleniumLibrary
    ${email}    Set Variable    test@example.com    # BuiltIn
    Input Text    id:email    ${email}    # SeleniumLibrary
    Sleep    500ms    # BuiltIn - Wait for form validation
    Click Button    id:register    # SeleniumLibrary
    Log    Registration completed    # BuiltIn
```

## Best Practices

### Logging
- Use Log liberally during development
- Include meaningful context: `Log    User: ${username}`
- Use log levels appropriately (INFO for normal, WARN for issues)
- Remove excessive logging in production tests

### Sleep
- Always include a reason: `Sleep    1s    API rate limit`
- Keep durations as short as necessary
- Prefer explicit waits when possible
- Document why the sleep is required

### Set Variable
- Use descriptive variable names: `${user_count}` not `${x}`
- Initialize variables close to where they're used
- Consider using Variables section for constants
- Use appropriate scope (test/suite/global)

Mastering BuiltIn keywords means understanding the fundamental building blocks that make Robot Framework tests work.
learningObjectives: Use Log keyword to output messages and variables for debugging
Understand Sleep keyword syntax and time format options
Create and assign variables with Set Variable keyword
Combine multiple BuiltIn keywords in sequential workflows
relatedConcepts: Log levels and visibility in reports

theory.title: Working with the String Library
theory.content:
## Robot Framework Standard Libraries

Beyond the BuiltIn library, Robot Framework includes several **standard libraries** that provide specialized functionality without requiring external installations. The **String library** is one of these, offering comprehensive text manipulation capabilities.

### Standard Libraries Overview

- **BuiltIn:** Always available (no import needed)
- **String:** Text manipulation and validation
- **Collections:** List and dictionary operations
- **OperatingSystem:** File and directory operations
- **DateTime:** Date and time handling
- **XML:** XML parsing and manipulation
- **Process:** Running external processes

## Importing Libraries

Libraries (except BuiltIn) must be imported in the `*** Settings ***` section before use.

### Import Syntax

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    LibraryName
Library    LibraryName    arg1    arg2
Library    path/to/custom_library.py
Library    LibraryName    WITH NAME    Alias
```

### String Library Import

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    String
```

After import, all String library keywords become available throughout the suite.

## The String Library

The String library provides keywords for:
- **Case conversion:** Upper, lower, title case
- **Validation:** Pattern matching, format checking
- **Manipulation:** Replace, strip, split, join
- **Generation:** Random strings, formatting

### Case Conversion Keywords

```robot
# Convert To Upper Case
${upper}    Convert To Upper Case    hello world
# Result: HELLO WORLD

# Convert To Lower Case
${lower}    Convert To Lower Case    HELLO WORLD
# Result: hello world

# Convert To Title Case
${title}    Convert To Title Case    hello world
# Result: Hello World
```

### String Manipulation Keywords

```robot
# Replace String
${result}    Replace String    Hello World    World    Robot
# Result: Hello Robot

# Strip String
${result}    Strip String    ${SPACE}${SPACE}text${SPACE}${SPACE}
# Result: text

# Split String
${parts}    Split String    a,b,c    separator=,
# Result: ['a', 'b', 'c']

# Get Substring
${sub}    Get Substring    Hello World    0    5
# Result: Hello
```

### String Validation Keywords

```robot
# Should Be String
Should Be String    ${variable}

# Should Be Lowercase
Should Be Lowercase    hello world

# Should Be Uppercase
Should Be Uppercase    HELLO WORLD

# Should Match Regexp
Should Match Regexp    test@example.com    ^[\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\.\w+$
```

## Converting to Upper Case

The `Convert To Upper Case` keyword transforms all characters in a string to uppercase.

### Syntax

```robot
${result}    Convert To Upper Case    string
```

**Parameter:**
- `string`: The text to convert (can be literal or variable)

### Examples

```robot
# Literal string
${upper}    Convert To Upper Case    hello
# Result: HELLO

# From variable
${text}     Set Variable    robot framework
${upper}    Convert To Upper Case    ${text}
# Result: ROBOT FRAMEWORK

# With special characters and numbers
${mixed}    Convert To Upper Case    Test123!@#
# Result: TEST123!@# (only letters affected)
```

### Use Cases

**Normalizing user input:**
```robot
${user_input}    Get User Input
${normalized}    Convert To Upper Case    ${user_input}
Should Be Equal    ${normalized}    EXPECTED VALUE
```

**Case-insensitive comparison:**
```robot
${actual_upper}      Convert To Upper Case    ${actual}
${expected_upper}    Convert To Upper Case    ${expected}
Should Be Equal      ${actual_upper}    ${expected_upper}
```

**Formatting display text:**
```robot
${heading}    Convert To Upper Case    ${section_title}
Log To Console    ${heading}
```

## Import, Use, Verify Pattern

This exercise demonstrates a fundamental Robot Framework pattern:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    String              # 1. Import the library

*** Test Cases ***
String Operations
    ${text}     Set Variable    robot framework    # 2. Prepare data
    ${upper}    Convert To Upper Case    ${text}    # 3. Use library keyword
    Log    ${upper}                                 # 4. Verify/output result
```

**This pattern applies to all libraries:**

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    Collections         # Import

*** Test Cases ***
List Operations
    ${items}    Create List    a    b    c    # Prepare
    ${length}   Get Length     ${items}       # Use
    Log    ${length}                          # Verify
```

## Settings Section Structure

The Settings section typically follows this order:

```robot
*** Settings ***
# 1. Documentation
Documentation    Suite description here

# 2. Metadata
Metadata         Version    1.0

# 3. Library imports
Library          String
Library          Collections
Library          SeleniumLibrary

# 4. Resource imports
Resource         ../resources/common.robot

# 5. Variables imports
Variables        ../configs/test_data.py

# 6. Suite lifecycle
Suite Setup      Initialize Environment
Suite Teardown   Cleanup Environment

# 7. Test lifecycle
Test Setup       Reset State
Test Teardown    Capture Screenshot On Failure

# 8. Tags
Force Tags       regression
Default Tags     string-operations
```

Order is **conventional**, not enforced, but following it improves readability.

## Library vs. BuiltIn Keywords

**BuiltIn keywords (no import needed):**
```robot
Log                  # BuiltIn
Set Variable         # BuiltIn
Should Be Equal      # BuiltIn
Sleep                # BuiltIn
```

**Library keywords (require import):**
```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    String
Library    Collections

*** Test Cases ***
Test
    Convert To Upper Case    text    # String library
    Get Length               list    # Collections library
```

If you use a library keyword without importing, you'll get:
```
No keyword with name 'Convert To Upper Case' found.
```

## Common String Library Use Cases

### Web Testing
```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    String
Library    SeleniumLibrary

*** Test Cases ***
Validate Username Format
    ${username}    Get Value    id:username-field
    ${lower}       Convert To Lower Case    ${username}
    Should Not Contain    ${lower}    ${SPACE}
    Should Match Regexp   ${lower}    ^[a-z0-9_]+$
```

### API Testing
```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    String
Library    RequestsLibrary

*** Test Cases ***
Validate API Response
    ${response}    GET    https://api.example.com/users
    ${json}        Convert To String    ${response.json()}
    Should Contain    ${json}    "status":"success"
```

### Data Processing
```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    String

*** Test Cases ***
Process CSV Data
    ${line}      Set Variable    John,Doe,john@example.com
    ${parts}     Split String    ${line}    ,
    ${email}     Get From List   ${parts}    2
    ${lower}     Convert To Lower Case    ${email}
    Should Match Regexp    ${lower}    ^[\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\.\w+$
```

## Best Practices

### Import Organization
- Group related libraries together
- Import only libraries you actually use
- Consider custom import names for clarity:
  ```robot
  Library    String    WITH NAME    Str
  ${upper}    Str.Convert To Upper Case    text
  ```

### Variable Naming
- Use descriptive names indicating type/purpose:
  ```robot
  ${upper_text}    Convert To Upper Case    ${text}
  ${normalized_email}    Convert To Lower Case    ${email}
  ```

### Chain Operations
```robot
# Less efficient: Multiple intermediate variables
${step1}    Strip String    ${input}
${step2}    Convert To Lower Case    ${step1}
${step3}    Replace String    ${step2}    _    -

# More efficient: Direct chaining
${result}    Strip String    ${input}
${result}    Convert To Lower Case    ${result}
${result}    Replace String    ${result}    _    -
```

By mastering library imports and the String library, you unlock powerful text manipulation capabilities essential for validation, data processing, and test automation.
learningObjectives: Import external libraries using the Settings section
Use String library keywords for text manipulation
Apply Convert To Upper Case for string transformation
Understand the distinction between BuiltIn and imported libraries

theory.title: Working with Lists Using the Collections Library
theory.content:
## Collections in Robot Framework

Robot Framework supports complex data structures like **lists** and **dictionaries**, enabling sophisticated test data management. The **Collections library** provides powerful keywords for manipulating these structures.

### Why Collections Matter

Simple variables store single values:
```robot
${user}    Set Variable    Alice
```

But real tests often need multiple related values:
```robot
# Testing with multiple users
@{users}    Create List    Alice    Bob    Charlie

# Testing with configuration data
&{config}    Create Dictionary    url=https://app.com    timeout=30
```

Collections enable **data-driven testing**, **iteration**, and **complex assertions**.

## List Variables in Robot Framework

### Syntax: Scalar vs. List Variables

**Scalar variables** (single value):
```robot
${name}    Set Variable    Alice
```

**List variables** (multiple values):
```robot
@{names}    Create List    Alice    Bob    Charlie
```

Notice:
- Scalar: `${variable_name}` (single item)
- List: `@{variable_name}` (collection)

### Creating Lists

**Using BuiltIn's Create List keyword:**
```robot
${fruits}    Create List    apple    banana    orange
```

Note: `Create List` returns a list, but you capture it in a **scalar variable** (`${fruits}`).

**Direct list variable definition:**
```robot
*** Variables ***
@{FRUITS}    apple    banana    orange
```

**Empty list:**
```robot
${empty}    Create List
```

### Accessing List Elements

```robot
${fruits}    Create List    apple    banana    orange

# By index (0-based)
${first}     Get From List    ${fruits}    0    # apple
${second}    Get From List    ${fruits}    1    # banana
${last}      Get From List    ${fruits}    -1   # orange

# Length
${count}     Get Length       ${fruits}        # 3
```

## The Collections Library

The Collections library extends BuiltIn's basic list/dictionary support with advanced operations.

### Import

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    Collections
```

### Key Collections Keywords

**List operations:**
```robot
Append To List        ${list}    item
Insert Into List      ${list}    index    item
Remove From List      ${list}    index
Get From List         ${list}    index
Get Slice From List   ${list}    start    end
Reverse List          ${list}
Sort List             ${list}
```

**Dictionary operations:**
```robot
Set To Dictionary     &{dict}    key=value
Get From Dictionary   &{dict}    key
Remove From Dictionary  &{dict}  key
Dictionary Should Contain Key    &{dict}    key
```

**Assertions:**
```robot
Should Contain        ${list}    item
List Should Contain Value        ${list}    item
Lists Should Be Equal            ${list1}   ${list2}
```

**Length operations:**
```robot
Get Length           ${list}
Length Should Be     ${list}    expected_length
```

## Get Length Keyword

The `Get Length` keyword (from Collections) returns the number of items in a collection.

### Syntax

```robot
${length}    Get Length    item
```

**Works with:**
- Lists: Number of items
- Dictionaries: Number of key-value pairs
- Strings: Number of characters

### Examples

```robot
# List length
${fruits}    Create List    apple    banana    orange
${count}     Get Length     ${fruits}
# Result: 3

# String length
${text}      Set Variable    hello
${length}    Get Length      ${text}
# Result: 5

# Dictionary length
${user}      Create Dictionary    name=Alice    age=30
${count}     Get Length           ${user}
# Result: 2

# Empty list
${empty}     Create List
${count}     Get Length    ${empty}
# Result: 0
```

## Using Lists in Tests

### Data-Driven Testing

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Test Multiple Users
    ${users}    Create List    alice    bob    charlie
    FOR    ${user}    IN    @{users}
        Login As User    ${user}
        Verify Dashboard Access
        Logout
    END
```

### Test Data Organization

```robot
*** Variables ***
@{VALID_EMAILS}      test@example.com    user@domain.org
@{INVALID_EMAILS}    invalid    @example.com    test@

*** Test Cases ***
Validate Email Format
    FOR    ${email}    IN    @{VALID_EMAILS}
        Email Should Be Valid    ${email}
    END
    
    FOR    ${email}    IN    @{INVALID_EMAILS}
        Email Should Be Invalid    ${email}
    END
```

### Assertions on Collections

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Validate Product List
    ${products}    Get Available Products
    ${count}       Get Length    ${products}
    Should Be True    ${count} > 0    No products available
    List Should Contain Value    ${products}    Premium Plan
```

## BuiltIn vs. Collections for Lists

### BuiltIn Keywords (No Import Needed)

```robot
# Create lists
${list}    Create List    item1    item2    item3

# Basic operations
${length}    Get Length    ${list}
Should Contain    ${list}    item1
```

### Collections Keywords (Require Import)

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    Collections

*** Test Cases ***
Advanced Operations
    ${list}    Create List    item1    item2    item3
    
    # Collections-specific keywords
    Append To List         ${list}    item4
    Insert Into List       ${list}    0    item0
    Remove From List       ${list}    1
    Reverse List           ${list}
    Sort List              ${list}
    
    # Advanced assertions
    List Should Contain Value          ${list}    item0
    List Should Not Contain Duplicates ${list}
```

**Rule of thumb:**
- Use **BuiltIn** for basic list creation and simple checks
- Use **Collections** for modification, sorting, and advanced assertions

## Complete Example: Testing with Lists

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    Collections

*** Variables ***
@{REQUIRED_FEATURES}    login    logout    profile    settings

*** Test Cases ***
Verify Application Features
    # Get features from application
    ${available_features}    Get Available Features
    
    # Verify count
    ${count}    Get Length    ${available_features}
    Should Be True    ${count} >= 4    Not enough features
    
    # Verify each required feature exists
    FOR    ${feature}    IN    @{REQUIRED_FEATURES}
        List Should Contain Value    ${available_features}    ${feature}
        ...    Feature '${feature}' not available
    END
    
    # Log for verification
    Log Many    @{available_features}

*** Keywords ***
Get Available Features
    # Mock implementation
    ${features}    Create List    login    logout    profile    settings    admin
    [Return]    ${features}
```

## List Best Practices

### Naming Conventions

```robot
# Clear, descriptive names
@{test_users}        alice    bob    charlie
@{valid_passwords}   Pass123!    Secret@456
@{product_ids}       100    200    300

# Avoid generic names
@{list1}    item1    item2    # Too generic
@{data}     x    y    z       # Not descriptive
```

### Initialization Location

```robot
# Suite-level constants: Variables section
*** Variables ***
@{BROWSERS}    Chrome    Firefox    Edge

# Test-specific data: Inside test case
*** Test Cases ***
Test With Dynamic Data
    ${users}    Create List    ${ADMIN}    ${USER1}
```

### Assertions

```robot
# Be explicit about expectations
${count}    Get Length    ${items}
Should Be Equal As Numbers    ${count}    3    Expected exactly 3 items

# Verify contents
List Should Contain Value    ${items}    expected_item
```

### Iteration

```robot
# Use FOR loops for repetitive operations
FOR    ${item}    IN    @{items}
    Process Item    ${item}
END
```

## Common Pitfalls

### Scalar vs. List Variable Syntax

```robot
# Wrong: Using @ when defining with Create List
@{fruits}    Create List    apple    banana    # Syntax error!

# Correct: Create List returns scalar
${fruits}    Create List    apple    banana

# Correct: Direct list definition
@{fruits}    apple    banana    orange
```

### Using Lists in Keywords

```robot
# Expanding list items as separate arguments
${items}    Create List    arg1    arg2    arg3
Keyword Name    @{items}    # Passes: arg1, arg2, arg3 as separate args

# Passing list as single argument
Keyword Name    ${items}    # Passes: [arg1, arg2, arg3] as one arg
```

By mastering lists and the Collections library, you unlock powerful data-driven testing capabilities essential for real-world test automation.
learningObjectives: Create lists using Create List keyword
Import and use the Collections library for advanced list operations
Determine list length with Get Length keyword
Understand the difference between scalar and list variables

theory.title: Creating Custom Keywords for Reusability
theory.content:
## Custom Keywords: The Foundation of Maintainable Tests

Custom keywords (also called **user keywords**) are user-defined functions that encapsulate test logic. They're Robot Framework's primary mechanism for creating **reusable**, **readable**, and **maintainable** test automation.

### Why Custom Keywords?

Without custom keywords:
```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Login Test 1
    Open Browser    https://app.com    Chrome
    Input Text      id:username        user1
    Input Text      id:password        pass1
    Click Button    id:login
    Page Should Contain    Dashboard
    Close Browser

Login Test 2
    Open Browser    https://app.com    Chrome
    Input Text      id:username        user2
    Input Text      id:password        pass2
    Click Button    id:login
    Page Should Contain    Dashboard
    Close Browser
```

**Problems:**
- Code duplication (DRY violation)
- Hard to maintain (change UI = update everywhere)
- Tests are verbose and hard to read

With custom keywords:
```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Login Test 1
    Login As User    user1    pass1
    Dashboard Should Be Visible

Login Test 2
    Login As User    user2    pass2
    Dashboard Should Be Visible

*** Keywords ***
Login As User
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    Open Browser       https://app.com    Chrome
    Input Text         id:username        ${username}
    Input Text         id:password        ${password}
    Click Button       id:login
    [Teardown]         Close Browser

Dashboard Should Be Visible
    Page Should Contain    Dashboard
```

**Benefits:**
- **DRY:** Logic defined once, used many times
- **Maintainable:** Change login process in one place
- **Readable:** Tests read like documentation
- **Abstraction:** Hide implementation details

## The Keywords Section

Custom keywords are defined in the `*** Keywords ***` section.

### Syntax

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Keyword Name
    Keyword Implementation
    More Keyword Steps
```

**Structure:**
- Keyword name: **No indentation**, starts at line beginning
- Keyword body: **4-space indentation** for all content
- Blank line separates different keywords

### Basic Custom Keyword

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Greet User
    Log    Welcome to Robot Framework!
```

**This keyword:**
- Name: `Greet User`
- Action: Logs a welcome message
- No arguments, no return value

### Calling Custom Keywords

Call custom keywords exactly like built-in keywords:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Test Custom Keyword
    Greet User    # Calls your custom keyword
```

Robot Framework automatically searches:
1. Built-in keywords
2. Imported library keywords
3. Custom keywords in current file
4. Custom keywords in imported resources

## Keyword Naming Conventions

### Descriptive, Action-Oriented Names

```robot
# Good names (verb-based, clear intent)
Login As User
Verify Dashboard Is Visible
Create New Account
Delete Test Data
Wait For Page Load

# Poor names
DoStuff
Test1
Keyword
Helper
```

### Naming Styles

**Title Case (recommended):**
```robot
Login As User
Verify Email Is Sent
```

**Snake Case:**
```robot
login_as_user
verify_email_is_sent
```

**Note:** Robot Framework is **case-insensitive** and **space/underscore-insensitive** for keyword names:

```robot
# All these call the same keyword
Login As User
login as user
LOGIN_AS_USER
login_as_user
LoginAsUser
```

Convention: Use **Title Case With Spaces** for readability.

## Simple Keywords Without Arguments

The simplest custom keywords take no arguments and perform a fixed action.

### Examples

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Initialize Test Environment
    Set Log Level    DEBUG
    Empty Directory    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/screenshots
    Log    Test environment initialized

Cleanup Test Data
    Delete All Test Users
    Clear Cache
    Log    Test data cleaned up

Print Test Header
    Log To Console    \n${'=' * 50}
    Log To Console    Starting Test Execution
    Log To Console    ${'=' * 50}\n
```

### When to Use Simple Keywords

- **Initialization/cleanup:** Setup and teardown operations
- **Utility functions:** Logging, reporting, formatting
- **Readability helpers:** Give descriptive names to complex operations
- **Repeated patterns:** Any operation used 3+ times

## Keyword Abstraction Levels

Custom keywords can call other keywords, creating abstraction layers.

### Low-Level Keywords (Implementation Details)

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Input Username
    [Arguments]    ${username}
    Input Text    id:username    ${username}

Input Password
    [Arguments]    ${password}
    Input Text    id:password    ${password}

Click Login Button
    Click Button    id:login
```

### Mid-Level Keywords (Common Operations)

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Login As User
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    Input Username    ${username}
    Input Password    ${password}
    Click Login Button
```

### High-Level Keywords (Business Workflows)

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Setup User Account
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    Navigate To Registration Page
    Register New User    ${username}    ${password}
    Verify Registration Email Sent
    Login As User    ${username}    ${password}
```

### Test Cases Use High-Level Keywords

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
User Registration And Login
    Setup User Account    testuser    Pass123!
    Dashboard Should Be Visible
    [Teardown]    Delete User Account    testuser
```

**Benefits:**
- Tests are **declarative** (what to do, not how)
- Implementation changes don't affect tests
- Easy to read by non-technical stakeholders

## Keywords in Practice

### Example: Web Testing

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    SeleniumLibrary

*** Test Cases ***
Successful Login
    Open Application
    Greet User
    Login As Admin
    Verify Dashboard
    [Teardown]    Close Application

*** Keywords ***
Open Application
    Open Browser    https://app.com    Chrome
    Maximize Browser Window

Greet User
    Log    Welcome to Robot Framework!
    Log To Console    Test starting...

Login As Admin
    Input Text      id:username    admin
    Input Text      id:password    secret123
    Click Button    id:login

Verify Dashboard
    Wait Until Page Contains    Dashboard    timeout=5s
    Page Should Contain Element    id:user-profile

Close Application
    Close All Browsers
```

### Example: API Testing

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    RequestsLibrary

*** Test Cases ***
Create And Verify User
    Greet User
    ${user_id}    Create Test User
    Verify User Exists    ${user_id}
    [Teardown]    Delete Test User    ${user_id}

*** Keywords ***
Greet User
    Log    Welcome to Robot Framework!

Create Test User
    ${response}    POST    https://api.example.com/users
    ...    json={"name": "Test User", "email": "test@example.com"}
    Should Be Equal As Numbers    ${response.status_code}    201
    ${user_id}    Set Variable    ${response.json()['id']}
    [Return]    ${user_id}

Verify User Exists
    [Arguments]    ${user_id}
    ${response}    GET    https://api.example.com/users/${user_id}
    Should Be Equal As Numbers    ${response.status_code}    200

Delete Test User
    [Arguments]    ${user_id}
    DELETE    https://api.example.com/users/${user_id}
```

## Best Practices

### 1. Single Responsibility

Each keyword should do **one thing well**:

```robot
# Good: Focused keywords
Login As User    ${username}    ${password}
Navigate To Settings
Update Profile Picture    ${image_path}

# Bad: Kitchen-sink keyword
Login And Update Profile    ${username}    ${password}    ${image}
```

### 2. Descriptive Names

Names should describe **what** the keyword does:

```robot
# Good
Verify Order Was Placed Successfully
Delete All Temporary Files

# Bad
Check Stuff
Do Cleanup
```

### 3. Appropriate Abstraction

Match abstraction level to usage:

```robot
# Test cases: High-level, business-oriented
*** Test Cases ***
User Can Purchase Product
    Add Product To Cart    Premium Plan
    Complete Checkout Process
    Verify Order Confirmation

# Keywords: Implementation details
*** Keywords ***
Complete Checkout Process
    Enter Shipping Information
    Enter Payment Information
    Click Place Order Button
```

### 4. Keyword Documentation

Document complex keywords:

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Verify Email Delivery
    [Documentation]    Checks that email was delivered within timeout period.
    ...                Polls email server every 5 seconds.
    ...                Fails if email not received within ${EMAIL_TIMEOUT}.
    [Arguments]    ${recipient}    ${subject}
    Wait Until Email Received    ${recipient}    ${subject}    ${EMAIL_TIMEOUT}
```

By mastering custom keywords, you transform test automation from repetitive scripts into **maintainable, readable, scalable** test suites.
learningObjectives: Create custom keywords in the Keywords section
Understand keyword naming conventions and syntax rules
Call custom keywords from test cases like built-in keywords
Recognize the benefits of keyword abstraction and reusability

theory.title: Parameterized Keywords with Arguments
theory.content:
## Arguments: Making Keywords Flexible and Reusable

While simple keywords (no arguments) are useful for fixed operations, **parameterized keywords** are where custom keywords truly shine. Arguments allow keywords to adapt to different inputs, making them genuinely reusable across diverse test scenarios.

### The Problem Without Arguments

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Greet Alice
    Log    Hello, Alice!

Greet Bob
    Log    Hello, Bob!

Greet Charlie
    Log    Hello, Charlie!
```

**Issues:**
- Massive code duplication
- New user = new keyword
- Impossible to scale

### The Solution: Arguments

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Greet Person
    [Arguments]    ${name}
    Log    Hello, ${name}!

# Usage
Greet Person    Alice
Greet Person    Bob
Greet Person    Charlie
```

**Benefits:**
- One keyword handles all cases
- Scalable to any number of names
- Follows DRY principle

## The [Arguments] Setting

The `[Arguments]` setting defines input parameters for a custom keyword.

### Syntax

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Keyword Name
    [Arguments]    ${arg1}    ${arg2}    ${arg3}
    # Keyword body using ${arg1}, ${arg2}, ${arg3}
```

**Rules:**
- `[Arguments]` must be the **first line** in keyword body (4-space indentation)
- Arguments separated by 4+ spaces
- Each argument is a variable: `${variable_name}`
- Arguments are **positional** (order matters)

### Basic Example

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Greet Person
    [Arguments]    ${name}
    Log    Hello, ${name}!
```

**Breakdown:**
- Keyword name: `Greet Person`
- Takes one argument: `${name}`
- Uses `${name}` in Log keyword

### Calling Keywords with Arguments

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Test Greetings
    Greet Person    Alice
    Greet Person    Bob
    Greet Person    ${USER_NAME}
```

Arguments are passed **positionally** after the keyword name, separated by 4+ spaces.

## Multiple Arguments

Keywords can accept multiple arguments.

### Definition

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Login As User
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    Input Text     id:username    ${username}
    Input Text     id:password    ${password}
    Click Button   id:login

Calculate Sum
    [Arguments]    ${a}    ${b}
    ${result}    Evaluate    ${a} + ${b}
    [Return]    ${result}

Create User
    [Arguments]    ${name}    ${email}    ${age}    ${role}
    Log    Creating user: ${name}
    Log    Email: ${email}, Age: ${age}, Role: ${role}
```

### Calling with Multiple Arguments

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Test Multiple Arguments
    Login As User    admin    secret123
    ${sum}    Calculate Sum    5    10
    Create User    Alice    alice@example.com    30    admin
```

**Argument mapping:**
```robot
Login As User    admin    secret123
                 ^         ^
              ${username} ${password}
```

## Using Arguments in Keyword Body

Arguments are regular variables—use them anywhere:

### In Strings

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Greet Person
    [Arguments]    ${name}
    Log    Hello, ${name}!
    Log    Welcome to the system, ${name}.
    Log To Console    User logged in: ${name}
```

### In Keyword Calls

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Login As User
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    Open Login Page
    Input Text        id:username    ${username}
    Input Text        id:password    ${password}
    Click Button      id:login
    Verify Login Success    ${username}

Verify Login Success
    [Arguments]    ${username}
    Page Should Contain    Welcome, ${username}
```

### In Assertions

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Verify User Age
    [Arguments]    ${age}
    Should Be True    ${age} >= 18    User must be 18 or older
    Should Be True    ${age} <= 120   Invalid age value
```

### In Return Values

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Get Full Name
    [Arguments]    ${first}    ${last}
    ${full}    Set Variable    ${first} ${last}
    [Return]    ${full}

# Usage
${name}    Get Full Name    John    Doe
Log    ${name}    # Logs: John Doe
```

## Variable Substitution in Arguments

Arguments can be:
- **Literal values:** `Greet Person    Alice`
- **Variables:** `Greet Person    ${USER_NAME}`
- **Expressions:** `Calculate Sum    ${X}    ${Y}`

```robot
*** Variables ***
${ADMIN_USER}    admin
${ADMIN_PASS}    secret123

*** Test Cases ***
Login Test
    # Using variables as arguments
    Login As User    ${ADMIN_USER}    ${ADMIN_PASS}
    
    # Using literals as arguments
    Login As User    testuser    testpass
    
    # Mixing both
    Login As User    ${ADMIN_USER}    testpass
```

## Argument Best Practices

### Descriptive Argument Names

```robot
# Good: Clear intent
Create User    ${username}    ${email}    ${role}

# Bad: Cryptic names
Create User    ${x}    ${y}    ${z}
```

### Logical Argument Order

```robot
# Good: Most important first
Login As User    ${username}    ${password}
Update Profile    ${user_id}    ${new_name}    ${new_email}

# Less intuitive
Login As User    ${password}    ${username}
```

### Consistent Naming

```robot
# Consistent across keywords
Create User       ${username}    ${password}
Delete User       ${username}
Verify User       ${username}

# Inconsistent (confusing)
Create User       ${username}    ${password}
Delete User       ${user}        # Different name for same concept
Verify User       ${name}        # Different name again
```

## Common Patterns

### Login Pattern

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Login As User
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    Open Browser       https://app.com    Chrome
    Input Text         id:username        ${username}
    Input Text         id:password        ${password}
    Click Button       id:login
    [Teardown]         Close Browser
```

### Verification Pattern

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Verify Element Contains Text
    [Arguments]    ${locator}    ${expected_text}
    ${actual_text}    Get Text    ${locator}
    Should Contain    ${actual_text}    ${expected_text}
```

### Data Creation Pattern

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Create Test User
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${email}    ${role}=user
    ${response}    POST    /api/users
    ...    json={"username": "${username}", "email": "${email}", "role": "${role}"}
    Should Be Equal As Numbers    ${response.status_code}    201
    [Return]    ${response.json()['id']}
```

## Real-World Example

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    SeleniumLibrary

*** Test Cases ***
Multiple User Login Tests
    Test Login For User    admin        secret123     Welcome, Admin
    Test Login For User    testuser     testpass      Welcome, Test User
    Test Login For User    invaliduser  wrongpass     Invalid credentials

*** Keywords ***
Test Login For User
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}    ${expected_message}
    Open Application
    Attempt Login    ${username}    ${password}
    Page Should Contain    ${expected_message}
    [Teardown]    Close Application

Attempt Login
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    Input Text      id:username    ${username}
    Input Text      id:password    ${password}
    Click Button    id:login

Open Application
    Open Browser    https://app.com    Chrome
    Maximize Browser Window

Close Application
    Close All Browsers
```

## Arguments vs. Variables Section

### When to Use Arguments (Keywords)

```robot
# Dynamic behavior, different per call
*** Keywords ***
Login As User
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    # Implementation
```

### When to Use Variables Section

```robot
# Static configuration, same across suite
*** Variables ***
${BASE_URL}     https://app.com
${TIMEOUT}      30
${ADMIN_USER}   admin
```

### Combining Both

```robot
*** Variables ***
${BASE_URL}    https://app.com

*** Keywords ***
Open Application Page
    [Arguments]    ${page_path}
    Open Browser    ${BASE_URL}${page_path}    Chrome

# Usage
Open Application Page    /login
Open Application Page    /dashboard
```

By mastering arguments, you create **flexible, reusable keywords** that adapt to different scenarios, making your test automation truly scalable and maintainable.
learningObjectives: Define keyword arguments using the [Arguments] setting
Pass arguments to custom keywords from test cases
Use argument variables within keyword implementation
Understand positional argument mapping and best practices
